FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 1.0
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.8
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` copies only the single `target_path` file into the temporary `tmpdir` sandbox, isolating it from the rest of the project workspace. 
FOLLOW: Because the evaluated file is isolated, any project-relative imports fail, causing `run_pyright` to detect massive `reportMissingImports` errors on the patched file. Furthermore, if `test_cmd` is executed with `cwd=tmpdir` (e.g., `pytest bench/tests/`), it immediately crashes with file-not-found errors because the test directory isn't copied into the sandbox. Consequently, `net_type_errors` spikes and `tests_passed` becomes `False`, forcing every proposed fix to be incorrectly marked `HARMFUL`. The fix evaluation pipeline is effectively dead.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Use `shutil.copytree()` to copy the entire current working directory into `tmpdir` (ignoring `.git` and `__pycache__`), then update `patched_path` to point to the relative target path within the sandboxed workspace. Temporarily `os.chdir(tmpdir)` while running the tools to ensure they resolve imports and test paths correctly within the isolated sandbox.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.85
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.5
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` omits `run_mypy` from both the pre-fix and post-fix issue counts, despite `run_mypy` being actively run in `scan_health()` to generate health signals for the insect brain.
FOLLOW: Since mypy errors are reported to the models as health diagnostics but explicitly ignored during fix evaluation, any fix that solely resolves a mypy error will yield `total_net == 0` and be evaluated as `NEUTRAL` (if tests aren't run). Conversely, a fix that introduces new mypy errors will not increase `total_net`, incorrectly allowing it to be marked `SAFE`. This creates a systemic blind spot that rejects valid typing fixes and admits broken ones.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Add `run_mypy` to the baseline and post-fix aggregations. Either sum its count into the existing `pre_type_errors` and `new_type_errors` variables alongside `run_pyright`, or track it as a separate `net_mypy_errors` metric incorporated into `total_net`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.75
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.3
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` arbitrarily defaults to returning `source_paths[0]` if it cannot match a filename from the finding's description text.
FOLLOW: If a finding describes a fix without explicitly mentioning a `.py` filename, it silently falls back to the first file in `source_paths`. If the proposed fix is a complete file replacement (Strategy 2 in `_apply_fix_to_source`), it will blindly overwrite `source_paths[0]` with code intended for a completely different module. This will catastrophically break the sandbox tests, leading to a spurious `HARMFUL` verdict while wasting compute resources evaluating the wrong file entirely.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Change the fallback in `_find_target_file()` to return `None` (or only fallback to the first file if `len(source_paths) == 1`). `evaluate_fix()` already safely handles a `None` target path by marking the fix as `UNEVALUABLE`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.50
FLAW_CLASS: 7
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.4
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` synchronously recalculates `pre_type_errors`, `pre_ruff_errors`, and `pre_bandit_issues` for the original `target_path` on every single finding evaluation.
FOLLOW: Static analysis tools take several seconds to run. If multiple findings target the same file (e.g., 10 findings for `endocrine.py`), the endocrine layer redundantly executes pyright, ruff, and bandit 10 times on the exact same unchanged baseline file. This needlessly blocks inter-round pacing, adding minutes of dead time to the verification cycle.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Cache the pre-fix tool counts in `evaluate_fixes()` using a dictionary keyed by `target_path`, and pass the cached baseline into `evaluate_fix()` to avoid redundant invocations.
VERIFIED: TRUE
